iii. Forestry (Forestry)

The rate of growth of forests remained 7.17 per cent. In increasing the rate of growth, the produce of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province is an important part.

iv. Fisheries (Fisheries)

The rate of growth of this sector remained 1.63 per cent, which is more than last year’s 1.23 per cent.

The production of the agricultural sector depends on the availability of water. According to the economic survey, the supply of water to both kharif and rabi crops was less than before. The government needs to take measures on a war footing to make the supply of water certain.

2. Industrial sector (Industrial Sector)

The share of the industrial sector in GDP is 20.87 per cent. The rate of growth of the industrial sector remained 5.80 per cent, which was 4.40 per cent in the last fiscal year. The provision of loans in the banking system, a better rate of interest, low inflation and strong internal demand are the important drivers of the speed of progress of the industrial sector. The further parts of the industrial sector are as follows:

i. Large-scale manufacturing sector (Large-scale manufacturing sector)

The share of this sector in industry is 80 per cent, while its share in GDP is 10.8 per cent. Among the sectors of large-scale production, deep freezers, jeeps, cars, cement, cloth, fertilisers, ghee, petroleum products and cigarettes etc. are included.

ii. Small-scale manufacturing sector (Small-scale Manufacturing Sector)

The share of this sector in industrial production is 13.8 per cent, while its share in GDP is 1.9 per cent. Carpet weaving, khaddar cloth, sheets, embroidered cloth, utensils, things made of wood and sports goods etc. belong to this sector.

iii. Slaughtering industry (Slaughtering Industry)

The share of this sector in industrial production is 6.5 per cent, while its share in GDP is 0.9 per cent. In this sector manufactures made from the hides and meat of animals are included.

iv. Mining (Mining and Quarrying)

The rate of growth of the mining sector is 3.04 per cent. Coal, natural gas, crude oil, chromite, gypsum and marble etc. are the important products of this sector.

3. Services sector (Service Sector)

The share of the services sector in GDP is 60.23 per cent, which was less than 60 per cent in the last fiscal year. The rate of growth of the services sector remained 6.43 per cent, which is more than the set target of 5.70 per cent. It has six sub-sectors:

(i) transport; (ii) means of communication; (iii) wholesale and retail trade; (iv) banking and insurance; (v) housing; (vi) services of the government and private sector.

paras.text: Foreign remittances are an important source of foreign exchange. Pakistan is counted among the countries that export labour. sections.content:
Per capita income is an important indicator for reviewing economic progress. Per capita income has increased by 0.5 per cent, and it has increased from last fiscal year’s 1,629 dollars to 1,641 dollars.

5. Saving and investment (Saving and Investment)

Allah Almighty has blessed Pakistan, along with mineral and natural resources, with mountains, deserts and fertile land. According to the economic survey, no change has come in the situation of saving and investment.

6. Foreign remittances (Foreign Remmittances)

Foreign remittances are an important source of foreign exchange. Pakistan is counted among the countries that export labour. In the months of July to March of the fiscal year 2017-18 an increase of 3.6 per cent occurred in foreign remittances, which was 2 per cent in the same period of the last fiscal year. Thus foreign remittances increased from last year’s 14.1 billion dollars to 14.6 billion dollars. Most of the remittances are received from Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Britain and America.

7. Inflation (Inflation)

The average of inflation remained 3.78 per cent, which was 4.01 per cent during the last fiscal year. From the reduction in the rate of inflation it is evident that reduction in prices is an important government priority.

8. Trade and payments (Trade and Payments)

During the last few years a decrease had been recorded in the exports of Pakistan, but since international markets are now being restored, improvement is visible in Pakistani exports too. Last year the decrease in exports was 12.2 per cent, which during this fiscal year is 1.76 per cent. The target of exports was set at 23.09 billion dollars, which could be obtained up to 14.8 billion dollars in the first nine months, which is 11.6 per cent more compared with last year.

On the other side the target of imports was fixed at 48.82 billion dollars. During the first eight months of the current fiscal year an increase of 17.1 per cent occurred in imports and the value of imports reached 33.4 billion dollars. To control the increasing imports, the government has imposed regulatory duty on imports.

The deficit of the current account during the first nine months became 12,029 million dollars, which in the same period of the last fiscal year was 7,990 million dollars.

9. Public debt (Public Debt)

Total public debt (up to February 2017) is 23,608 billion rupees, while government debt is 21,552 billion rupees. An increase of 1,093 billion rupees occurred in internal debt, while an increase of 1,107 billion rupees was recorded in external debt.

10. Education sector (Education Sector)

There are three basic measures for judging the standard of education: (i) enrolment rate; (ii) number of educational institutions; (iii) number of teachers. In these three, during the current fiscal year, slight improvement has been seen. In 2016-17 total enrolment was 48.062 million, which during 2015-16 was 46.223 million. Thus an increase of 3.97 per cent occurred in enrolment. During 2017-18 this number is expected to be 50.426 million.

کرنٹ اکاؤنٹ کا خسارہ پہلے نو ماہ کے دوران 12,029 ملین ڈالر ہو گیا، جو کہ پچھلے مالی سال کے اسی عرصہ میں 7,990 ملین ڈالر تھا۔

9۔ سرکاری قرض: (Public Debt)

کل سرکاری قرض (فروری 2017ء تک) 23,608 بلین روپے ہے جبکہ حکومتی قرض 21,552 بلین روپے ہے۔ اندرونی قرضے میں 1,093 بلین روپے کا اضافہ ہوا جبکہ بیرونی قرضے میں 1,107 بلین روپے کا اضافہ ریکارڈ کیا گیا۔

10۔ تعلیم کا شعبہ: (Education Sector)

معیارِ تعلیم جانچنے کے لیے تین بنیادی پیمانے ہیں: (i) انرولمنٹ ریٹ (ii) تعلیمی اداروں کی تعداد (iii) اساتذہ کی تعداد۔ ان تینوں میں موجودہ مالی سال کے دوران معمولی بہتری دیکھنے میں آئی ہے۔ 2016-17ء میں کل انرولمنٹ 48.062 ملین تھی، جو کہ 2015-16ء کے دوران 46.223 ملین تھی۔ اس طرح انرولمنٹ میں 3.97 فی صد اضافہ ہوا۔ 2017-18ء کے دوران یہ تعداد 50.426 ملین ہونے کی توقع ہے۔
